Amid the fanfare of trumpets, the piercing notes of a steam caliope, the prancing of horses, the squealing of monkeys and the roaring of lions, Jackie Coogan runs away and joins a circus in his latest picture, "Circus Days," which comes to the Queen's Theatre to-day for an engagement of five days.
Heralded as the finest picture that the inimitable Jackie has yet made, it is the sort of story that should appeal to every boy or girl—young or old.

Driven from home and his widowed mother, Toby Tyler, the youthful hero played by the star, starts his adventures under the "big top" as a peanut salesman. His vicissitudes are many, but Dame Fortuna finally looks upon him with favour, and through a sudden accident Toby finds himself the star of the circus, and the one big hero of the sawdust
